subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw accept SKILL.md-declared schedule/event triggers as an executable public contract, and under what approval and trust boundary?
rationale: The request would let skill metadata influence autonomous scheduling and event-triggered agent execution, which crosses public skill API, scheduler ownership, ClawHub trust, and security-review boundaries that code cannot infer safely.

options.title: Support permissioned trigger metadata
options.body: Adopt a namespaced trigger contract with explicit operator approval, audit state, revocation behavior, and docs before wiring it into cron or events.

options.title: Allow descriptive metadata only
options.body: Add non-executable trigger_description or indexing metadata while keeping actual scheduling in explicit cron jobs or standing-order configuration.

options.title: Defer to plugin and ClawHub work
options.body: Keep this issue open under the broader skill trust/API roadmap until plugin hooks and ClawHub permission metadata can own the execution model.

recommendation.title: Support permissioned trigger metadata
recommendation.body: Adopt a namespaced trigger contract with explicit operator approval, audit state, revocation behavior, and docs before wiring it into cron or events.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision affects the skill metadata loader and prompt contract history where this owner has the strongest observed provenance.
